title: Entanglement Mpemba Effect
abstract: Generating entanglement rapidly and reliably is essential for quantum information processing, communication, and metrology. Dissipative preparation is attractive because engineered reservoirs robustly drive a system toward an entangled target, yet relaxation can carry a substantial time cost. Here we formulate the entanglement Mpemba effect, whereby an initially less entangled state overtakes a more entangled state under the same open-system dynamics. This effect turns initial-state engineering into a route for faster preparation without altering the dissipative protocol. We derive a general criterion for the reversal from the relaxation spectrum, applicable even when entanglement evolves nonmonotonically. A reversal of deterministic local operations and classical communication (LOCC)-reachability preorder provides a measure-independent certificate of reversed entanglement order. Exactly solvable models show that initial-state selection can substantially shorten the time required to reach high entanglement. We further propose an experimentally relevant trapped-ion protocol that can realize the entanglement Mpemba effect.
summary: The paper introduces the entanglement Mpemba effect, demonstrating that an initially less entangled state can surpass a more entangled one under constant open-system evolution. It derives rigorous spectral criteria based on system dynamics and proposes this phenomenon as a method to significantly speed up the preparation of highly entangled quantum states using trapped ions.
main_problem: The paper investigates the 'entanglement Mpemba effect,' determining if an initially less entangled quantum state can overtake a more entangled state while both evolve under identical open-system dynamics.
main_result: The effect is characterized by a spectral criterion derived from the asymptotic behavior of entanglement differences, and it provides a route for faster preparation of high entanglement via initial-state engineering.
method: Theoretical analysis involving the Liouville expansion to derive asymptotic comparison spectra for entanglement monotones, supplemented by an LOCC reachability preorder certificate.
model_or_system: General finite-dimensional multipartite quantum systems evolving under time-homogeneous open dynamics governed by a Lindblad dissipator. Specific realizations include two- and three-qubit models and trapped-ion protocols.
key_observables: Entanglement monotones (e.g., concurrence, negativity), the ordering difference $\Delta E(t)$, and the first hitting time to an entanglement threshold.
important_parameters: Decay rates ($r$), amplitudes ($K_E$), and Jordan-block powers ($q_E$) derived from the asymptotic expansion of the state evolution.
main_assumptions: The spectral criterion is sufficient but not necessary for the Mpemba effect; the analysis assumes a common branch where the exponential expansion applies.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the construction of quantum pumps for two- and three-qubit systems, showing how different decay rates select active faces, and demonstrating that entanglement measures like concurrence and negativity reverse their initial ordering.
paper_structure: The paper first formulates the problem using general open dynamics, derives a spectral criterion based on asymptotic expansion, establishes the LOCC preorder certificate, applies these tools to exactly solvable models (2-qubit/3-qubit), and concludes with an experimentally relevant trapped-ion protocol realization.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges non-equilibrium thermodynamics (the Mpemba effect) with quantum information theory by showing how initial state engineering can accelerate the approach to entangled steady states in open quantum systems, which is highly relevant for quantum control and computation.

(b) The same construction pumps a product source and an orthogonal GHZ state into a common GHZ attractor. In both cases all channels are present for both preparations; the initial support selects the active one.

FIG. 3. The initially less-entangled fast state overtakes the slow state for both genuine multipartite concurrence and the minimum normalized one-versus-two cut negativity. The two measures follow inequivalent fast branches.

FIG. 2. (a) Concurrence and normalized negativity reverse their initial ordering at different times under the same gen- erator. (b) The ratios of the individual deficits decay with the visible-rate difference γf −γs, as predicted by the spectral criterion.
